headline: Two Boston officers hospitalized after Blackstone Square arrest, police say
dek: Police say a Cambridge man punched an officer and fought with officers after multiple people reported being assaulted in the South End park; the suspect pleaded not guilty in court.
body: Two Boston police officers were taken to a hospital with non-life-threatening injuries after trying to arrest a man accused of assaulting several people at Blackstone Square in the South End. The incident began Monday, Oct. 12, at about 5:34 p.m. near 1535 Washington St., according to the [Boston Police Department’s account](https://police.boston.gov/2026/10/13/violent-suspect-arrested-after-assaulting-multiple-victims-and-officers-in-blackstone-square/).

The department said officers assigned to District D-4 were responding to a report of an assault and battery in progress. Dispatch information described a masked man who was assaulting people and trying to kick multiple dogs inside the park. Several people pointed officers toward a suspect when they arrived, police said. The account released by police describes allegations and witness reports; it does not establish guilt.

According to police, the man walked away while officers gave commands and kept his hands obscured. He allegedly rolled up his sleeves, took a fighting stance near 35 W. Newton St. and tried to enter a building. As officers attempted to stop him, police say he punched one officer in the face. Another officer used a Taser, but the department said the man recovered and continued resisting before additional officers and civilians helped take him into custody.

Police later spoke with people who said they had been targeted before the struggle. One person reported that the suspect knocked a cellphone from his hand, picked it up and ran; officers recovered the phone and returned it, according to the department. A second person said the man grabbed his wrist, demanded his watch, followed him farther into the park after he refused and shoved and punched him. A dog walker reported being threatened.

The department identified the arrested man as Sharkell Tariq Matthews, 26, of Cambridge. Police listed charges of unarmed assault to rob, two counts of assault and battery on a police officer, assault and battery on an elderly person, assault and resisting arrest. [NBC Boston reported](https://www.nbcboston.com/news/local/boston-police-officer-assault-south-end/4030665/) that Matthews appeared in court, pleaded not guilty and was represented by an attorney who said he is unhoused. Matthews was also taken to a hospital for evaluation, NBC reported.

The two officers taken to the hospital were the first officers to reach the scene, the police department said. Officials did not identify them or describe the specific injuries beyond saying they were not life-threatening. The initial police release also did not name the people who reported being assaulted or say whether any of them required medical treatment. No firearm was mentioned in the department’s account of the arrest.

The confrontation has unsettled people who use Blackstone Square and the surrounding South End streets. NBC Boston reported that police planned to increase patrols in the area after the incident. City Councilor Ed Flynn, who represents the neighborhood, told the station he wants tougher punishment for people who hurt first responders. That response reflects the neighborhood concern, but it is separate from the court’s eventual assessment of the charges.

The next phase is the criminal case, where prosecutors must prove each allegation and the defense can contest the police account and witness statements. The available accounts leave some questions unanswered, including the full sequence involving the civilian witnesses, the officers’ specific injuries and what treatment Matthews received. For now, the confirmed public record is an arrest, a not-guilty plea, two hospitalized officers and a case moving through Boston Municipal Court.
location: Blackstone Square and 35 W. Newton Street, South End, Boston, Massachusetts
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Two Boston officers hospitalized after Blackstone Square arrest
seoDescription: Boston police say two officers suffered non-life-threatening injuries while arresting a Cambridge man accused of assaults at Blackstone Square in the South End.
